title: Publish a ChatGPT canvas
metaTitle: Publish a ChatGPT canvas as a website · Aero
description: Put a page you made in ChatGPT online at its own address. Paste one prompt from Aero into the chat, or save the code as index.html and upload it.
answer: To publish a ChatGPT canvas, copy one prompt from Aero into the ChatGPT chat where you made the page and send it. The prompt tells ChatGPT to publish the files to Aero and reply with the live link. Or save the code as index.html and upload it.
needs: The ChatGPT chat where you made the page

steps.name: Start a new site from a prompt
steps.text: In Aero, go to Sites, New site, and pick From Claude or ChatGPT.

steps.name: Copy the prompt
steps.text: Press Copy prompt. Copying it adds your personal publish key, so keep the prompt to yourself, like a password.

steps.name: Paste it into your ChatGPT chat
steps.text: Go back to the chat where you made the page, paste the prompt and send it. ChatGPT publishes the files to Aero and replies with the live link.

steps.name: Open the site in Aero
steps.text: Aero sees the site go live and says so. Press Done to open its page: the address, a preview and its versions.

alt.p: Copy the code from the canvas into a text file and save it as index.html. Then go to New site, Upload HTML, drop the file in and press Publish.

gets: A live site at its own aeroapp.ai address
A copy of your page. Your chat stays as it was
Versions you can go back to
On the free plan, sites stay live for 7 days
faq: Does my page stay in ChatGPT?
Yes. Aero publishes a copy at its own address. Your chat stays as it was.
How do I update the site?
Ask ChatGPT for the change in the same chat. On the site’s page, Ask Claude or ChatGPT gives you a prompt that publishes the next version to the same address. Aero keeps the old versions.
Can I keep it private?
Add a password on Basic and up, so only people you give it to can open it.
How long does a free site stay live?
7 days, counted from when your first site goes live. Then it goes offline and keeps its address. Paid plans keep sites live, from $3 a month with a 7-day free trial.
Can I test it with people?
Yes. On the site’s page, press Test this site. You get a test link to send to anyone.

title: Publish a Lovable app
metaTitle: Publish a Lovable app on its own address · Aero
description: Aero publishes the built files of a Lovable app. Export the code, build it, drop the output folder in, and it’s live at its own aeroapp.ai address.
answer: To publish a Lovable app on Aero, get your project’s code out of Lovable, build it into static files, and drop the folder or a zip of it into Aero. There is no Lovable integration. Or open the project in a coding agent and paste Aero’s publish prompt.
needs: Your project’s code, out of Lovable
Node.js on your computer, to build it (or a coding agent that does it for you)

steps.name: Get the code out of Lovable
steps.text: Export the project’s code from Lovable, for example through its GitHub connection, and put it in a folder on your computer.

steps.name: Build it into static files
steps.text: Lovable projects are code, not finished pages, so they need a build first. In the project folder, run npm run build. The output folder (often called dist) is what Aero hosts.

steps.name: Start a new site in Aero
steps.text: Go to Sites, New site, and pick Upload HTML.

steps.name: Drop in the build folder
steps.text: Drop the build folder, or a zip of it, with index.html at the top. The name is optional: leave it blank and the site is named after its address.

steps.name: Publish and open the site
steps.text: Press Publish. The site is live in seconds and Aero opens its page: the address, a preview and its versions.

alt.h: Prefer to let a coding agent do it?
alt.p: Open the project in Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. In Aero, go to New site, From Claude or ChatGPT, copy the prompt and paste it there. The prompt tells the agent to build the project, zip the output and send it to Aero. Nothing to install.

gets: A live site at its own aeroapp.ai address
A static copy of your build. The project in Lovable doesn’t change
Every version kept, so you can go back
On the free plan, sites stay live for 7 days
faq: Is there a Lovable integration?
No. Aero doesn’t connect to Lovable. You export the code, build it, and upload the result, or let a coding agent do those steps.
Does my Lovable project change?
No. Aero hosts a copy of the built files. Your project in Lovable stays as it is.
How do I update the site?
Change the project and build it again. On the site’s page, drop the new folder on Drop files. It becomes the next version at the same address, and Aero keeps the old ones.
Can I keep it private?
Add a password on Basic and up, so only people you give it to can open it.
How long does a free site stay live?
7 days, counted from when your first site goes live. Then it goes offline and keeps its address. Paid plans keep sites live, from $3 a month with a 7-day free trial.

title: Publish a Figma prototype
metaTitle: Publish a Figma prototype at its own address · Aero
description: Turn a Figma prototype link into a site at its own aeroapp.ai address. Share the prototype, paste the link into Aero, and send the address.
answer: To publish a Figma prototype, share it in Figma so anyone with the link can view it, then paste its link into a new site in Aero. You get a site at its own address that shows the live prototype.
needs: The prototype shared so anyone with the link can view it

steps.name: Share the prototype in Figma
steps.text: In your Figma file, click Share and choose Anyone and View. Aero checks the link for you and, if it can’t be opened yet, shows you how to share it.

steps.name: Start a new site from Figma
steps.text: In Aero, go to Sites, New site, and pick From Figma.

steps.name: Paste the link
steps.text: Paste your prototype link into the All screens row. If you paste a design or file link instead, Aero turns it into a prototype link and says so.

steps.name: Add other screen sizes (optional)
steps.text: Add breakpoint lets you give phones or tablets their own link. Leave it and one link serves every screen.

steps.name: Create the site
steps.text: The name is optional. Press Create site and Aero opens the site’s page with its address. Send the address to anyone.

alt.h: Want real HTML instead of an embed?
alt.p: Under Other ways on the same screen, Convert with AI gives you a prompt for Claude or ChatGPT. It reads your design through the Figma connector, builds the page and publishes it to Aero. It needs the Figma connector, and a Dev or Full seat on a paid Figma plan gives the most room. Or build real code with pxCode.

gets: A site at its own address that shows your live Figma prototype
Changes you make in Figma show up on their own
Separate links for phones or tablets, if you add them
On the free plan, sites stay live for 7 days
faq: Does the Figma file need to be public?
The prototype needs to be viewable by anyone with the link. Sharing is about access: the link decides which screen opens first.
Does Aero copy my design?
No. The site shows your live prototype from Figma. Nothing is converted unless you choose Convert with AI or pxCode.
Can I keep it private?
Add a password on Basic and up, so only people you give it to can open it.
How long does a free site stay live?
7 days, counted from when your first site goes live. Then it goes offline and keeps its address. Paid plans keep sites live, from $3 a month with a 7-day free trial.
Can I test it with people?
Yes. Start a new test, pick From Figma and paste the same link. You get a test link to send to anyone.

title: User test a Figma prototype
metaTitle: User test a Figma prototype with a link · Aero
description: Run a think-aloud test on a Figma prototype. Paste the link into Aero, add tasks, send the test link, and get recordings, transcripts and summaries back.
answer: To user test a Figma prototype, paste its link into a new test in Aero, add a few tasks, and send the test link. Testers talk through it, and you get the recording, transcript and summary back.
needs: A Figma prototype shared so anyone with the link can view it
A few people to send the link to

steps.name: Share the prototype in Figma
steps.text: Click Share, choose Anyone and View. Aero checks this when you paste the link.

steps.name: Start a new test from Figma
steps.text: In Aero, go to Tests, start a new test, and pick From Figma. Paste your prototype link and press Create test.

steps.name: Add tasks (optional)
steps.text: Add a few short tasks, like “Find your cards”. With no tasks, testers explore freely and the review sums up the whole session.

steps.name: Send the test link
steps.text: Press Copy test link and send it to your testers. On a computer, Aero records their tab and voice. On a phone, their voice only.

steps.name: Review the sessions
steps.text: Each session shows up in Sessions when the tester finishes. The transcript and summary follow: about a minute for a short session, longer for a long one.

alt.h: Already published the prototype as a site?
alt.p: Start a new test and pick One of your sites. The test uses that site.

gets: A recording of the tester’s browser tab and their voice
A transcript and a summary of each session, with the moments they got stuck
Insights across sessions once two are analysed
A test link that works without an account
faq: Do testers need an account?
No. They open the test link, allow their microphone and the tab, and start.
Does Aero find testers for me?
No. Bring your own testers: friends, clients, colleagues or classmates.
What is recorded?
The tester’s browser tab and their voice. Never their camera, and not their mouse pointer.
Can people test on a phone?
A Figma prototype test works on a phone and records their voice only. A site or HTML test needs a computer, because Aero records the tab.
How many sessions do I get?
Free has 3 test sessions, Basic 5, Solo 10 and Pro 20. They are a total on your plan, not a monthly allowance. Transcripts and summaries are on every plan.

title: Watch a user test recording
metaTitle: Watch a user test recording · Aero
description: Open a finished session in Aero and watch what the tester did on screen while they talked. Change the speed, skip silence and go full screen.
answer: To watch a user test recording, open Tests, pick the test, then Sessions, and open a session. The recording plays with the tester’s voice. You can change the speed, skip silence and jump to any task.
needs: A test with at least one finished session

steps.name: Open the session
steps.text: Go to Tests, open your test, then Sessions. Pick a session from the list.

steps.name: Press play
steps.text: The recording and the tester’s voice play together. Space plays and pauses. The arrow keys move 5 seconds.

steps.name: Change how you watch
steps.text: Pick a speed from the Speed menu. Turn on Skip to jump over pauses longer than 2 seconds; the timeline shortens to match. Use the full screen button for a bigger view.

steps.name: Jump to a moment
steps.text: Hover a mark on the timeline to read it and click it to play from there. Press a task’s start time in the Summary tab to play from that task.

steps.name: Check the details
steps.text: Details in the Summary tab show when it ran, its length, the device and screen size, and how the tester rated difficulty, when they gave a rating.

gets: The screen recording with the tester’s voice
The tester’s tasks, with done or couldn’t do it and the time spent
A Download menu for the video, audio and transcript
faq: Does it show the tester’s face?
No. Aero records the screen and the voice. The camera is never used.
Does it show their mouse?
No. A browser-tab recording doesn’t show the mouse.
What if the tester was on a phone?
Phones can’t share a tab, so a Figma test on a phone records their voice only. The session says so.
Can I delete a recording?
Yes. Delete session is in the Download menu. It removes the recording, the transcript and the summary for good.

alt.p: Read the summary first. It is written from the transcript, so you know where to look before you press play.

title: Get a transcript of a user test
metaTitle: Get a transcript of a user test · Aero
description: Every Aero session is transcribed after the tester finishes. Read it beside the recording, click a line to jump, or download it as a text file.
answer: To get a transcript of a user test, open the session in Aero and pick Transcript. It arrives after the tester finishes: about a minute for a short session, longer for a long one.
facts: About a minute after a short session
needs: A session where the tester’s microphone was on

steps.name: Wait for it to arrive
steps.text: The transcript follows after the tester finishes, never during. Until then the session says Transcript arriving, and the recording is ready to watch.

steps.name: Open the Transcript tab
steps.text: Open the session and pick Transcript next to Summary. Turn on Follow the recording to have it scroll as the recording plays.

steps.name: Click a line
steps.text: Click any line to play the recording from that point.

steps.name: Download it
steps.text: Open the Download menu and pick Transcript (.txt). You can also download the video and audio there.

gets: A transcript of what the tester said, in their own words
Lines that follow the recording and jump to it
A summary written from the transcript
faq: How long does a transcript take?
About a minute for a short session, longer for a long one.
Is it live while the tester talks?
No. It arrives after they finish.
What if the microphone was off?
Then there is no transcript or summary. The recording and the tasks still count.
What if the tester said nothing?
The transcript comes back empty and the session says so. The recording and the tasks still count.
Does it cost extra?
No. Transcripts and summaries are on every plan, Free included.

title: Find what to fix first from several user tests
metaTitle: Find what to fix first across user test sessions · Aero
description: Insights puts your sessions together: a summary, up to 5 numbered fixes ranked by severity, how many testers hit each one, and their quotes.
answer: To find what to fix first, open your test in Aero and pick Insights. Once two sessions are analysed, it puts them together: a short summary and up to 5 numbered fixes, ranked by severity and by how many testers hit them.
needs: A test with at least 2 sessions that have a finished summary

steps.name: Run two or more sessions
steps.text: Insights start once two sessions are analysed. Before that, the tab tells you what it is waiting for.

steps.name: Open Insights
steps.text: Go to Tests, open your test, then Insights. If it has not started, press Build insights.

steps.name: Read what to fix first
steps.text: Each fix is numbered, with its severity (Critical, Major or Minor), a suggested fix and how many testers hit it, such as “2 of 3 testers”.

steps.name: Play the quotes
steps.text: Quote cards under a fix show the tester, the time and their words. Press play to hear the moment.

steps.name: Check the themes
steps.text: Recurring themes group what came up in more than one session. Where testers disagreed shows both sides and who said what, and What worked lists what went well.

steps.name: Update it as sessions arrive
steps.text: New sessions join in about a minute. If some are not included yet, press Update now.

gets: A short summary across your sessions
Up to 5 numbered fixes, most serious first
Quotes you can play, from the testers who hit each one
Recurring themes, where testers disagreed, and what worked
faq: How many sessions does it need?
At least 2 that have been analysed.
Is there an upper limit?
Aero reads your 40 newest sessions. The line at the top says “Based on N of M sessions”.
How do I know which sessions it used?
The line at the top shows how many it used and when it was last updated. In this summary lists the sessions.
Do my own preview runs count?
No. Preview as tester runs show as You and stay out of Insights.
Can I edit the fixes?
Not the fixes themselves. In a session you can change a finding’s label or mark it Not a finding, and its quote then stops showing here.

title: Review a user test session on a timeline
metaTitle: Review a user test session on a timeline · Aero
description: One track shows the tester’s voice, your tasks and a mark for each finding. Hover a mark to read it, click to play. Lanes splits them into rows.
answer: To review a session on a timeline, open it in Aero and look under the recording. One track shows the tester’s voice with a mark for each finding. Hover a mark to read it and click to play from there.

steps.name: Open the session
steps.text: Go to Tests, open your test, then Sessions, and pick a session.

steps.name: Read the track
steps.text: One track is the default: a faint waveform of the tester’s voice, your tasks as regions, and a label icon for each finding. A warning triangle is an issue, a question mark is confusion, a lightbulb is a request and a tick is something that works well.

steps.name: Jump around
steps.text: Click or drag the timeline to move the recording. Hover a mark to read it and click it to play from there.

steps.name: Filter the marks
steps.text: Under the track, pick All, Issues, Confusion, Works well or Requests to show one kind.

steps.name: Try Lanes
steps.text: Switch Timeline view to Lanes to give tasks, voice and quotes their own rows. Its Summary switch can show the summary above them.

steps.name: Change a label
steps.text: If you disagree with a finding, use its label button in the Summary tab to change its kind or severity, or mark it Not a finding. It shows “Changed by you”, and Back to the original undoes it.

gets: Tasks on a timeline, with done or couldn’t do it
Findings marked at the moment they were said
A view for watching and a view for reading
faq: Is that a waveform?
Yes, a faint one of the tester’s voice. Older sessions show when the tester was talking instead.
Does the timeline show the tester’s mouse?
No. Browser-tab recordings show no mouse.
Does changing a label change the analysis?
No. Your change is kept beside it and shown as “Changed by you”. The analysis itself is never edited.
Why are some task times marked as estimated?
Older sessions have task times that are a few seconds out. The session says so.
Can I add my own marks?
Not today.

alt.p: Switch to Read view for a page you read like an article: the summary, tasks, then the transcript, with a small recording in the corner.

title: Send a user test link with no account needed
metaTitle: Send a user test link, no account needed · Aero
description: Copy a test link from Aero and send it to anyone. They open it, allow the microphone and the tab, and talk as they go. No sign-up for them.
answer: To send a user test link, open your test in Aero, press Copy test link and send it to anyone. They open it, allow their microphone and the tab, and start. They don’t need an Aero account.
needs: A few people to send the link to

steps.name: Copy the link
steps.text: Open your test and press Copy test link at the top, or Copy link in Setup. Send it by email, chat or anywhere else.

steps.name: What they see first
steps.text: Who asked them, what happens, what is recorded (their voice and this tab, never the camera) and that they can stop at any time. They can add their first name, or leave it blank.

steps.name: Allow recording
steps.text: One card, Allow recording, has a Microphone row and a Screen recording row, each with Allow. In Chrome’s list they pick this tab, then press Share. Nothing is recorded until they press Start the test.

steps.name: Let them run it
steps.text: They try the tasks in a small panel they can drag anywhere, talk as they go, and press Finish. They see Thank you straight away while the last part saves.

steps.name: Close the link
steps.text: Switch off Taking new sessions in Setup when you have enough. Testers who open the link then see a closed message, and the sessions you have stay.

gets: A recording, transcript and summary for each tester
One link you can send to as many people as you like
A switch to stop new sessions when you have enough
faq: Does the tester need an Aero account?
No. They open the link and start.
Does it use their camera?
No. Aero records the screen and the voice.
Can people test on a phone?
A Figma prototype test works on a phone and records their voice only. A site or HTML test needs a computer, because Aero records the tab.
How many sessions can I run?
Free has 3 test sessions, Basic 5, Solo 10 and Pro 20. Your own Preview as tester runs don’t count.
Does Aero find testers for me?
No. Bring your own testers.

alt.h: Want to try it yourself first?
alt.p: Press Preview as tester at the top of the test. Your own runs show as You, don’t use up your sessions and stay out of Insights.

title: Write user test tasks
metaTitle: Write user test tasks testers understand · Aero
description: Tasks are optional in Aero. Add them in the test’s Setup, give each a short description if it helps, and testers see them in a panel as they go.
answer: To write user test tasks in Aero, open your test, go to Setup, type a task in Add a task and press Enter. Write the goal, not the clicks. Tasks are optional: without them, testers explore freely.

steps.name: Open Setup
steps.text: Go to Tests, open your test, then Setup. Tasks have their own section.

steps.name: Add a task
steps.text: Type what they should try in Add a task and press Enter. For example: “Send £20 to Maya”. Example.

steps.name: Add a description if needed
steps.text: Open the task’s menu and pick Edit. Add a short description, such as “Start from the home screen”, then press Save or Enter. Esc cancels.

steps.name: Keep each task to one thing
steps.text: Write the goal, not the clicks. Short tasks are easier to say aloud and easier to review.

steps.name: Order and remove
steps.text: Drag a task by its handle to reorder it, or hold Alt and press the arrow keys. Delete is in the task’s menu, with Undo straight after.

gets: Tasks shown to the tester in a panel while they test
Done or couldn’t do it, with time spent, for each task in the session
Task regions on the review timeline
faq: Do I need tasks?
No. Without any, testers explore freely.
How many tasks should I write?
A few short ones. When Claude sets up a test from a prompt, it asks you for 1 to 5.
Can I ask testers to rate difficulty?
Yes. Switch on Difficulty rating in Setup and testers rate each task after they finish it.
Can I change the welcome and thank-you messages?
Yes. Messages in Setup has both. Edit one, press Save, and Show how this looks previews it.
Can I turn off voice or screen recording?
Setup has switches for Record audio and Record screen.

title: Password-protect a prototype
metaTitle: Password-protect a prototype · Aero
description: Add a password to a site in Aero so only people you give it to can open it. Set it in the site’s Settings. Needs the Basic plan or above.
answer: To password-protect a prototype in Aero, open its site, type a password of 6 or more characters under Password in Settings, press Set password, then turn the switch on. Needs Basic or above.

steps.name: Open the site
steps.text: Go to Sites and open the site. Its Settings sit beside the Site, Versions and Analytics tabs (below them on a phone).

steps.name: Find Password
steps.text: On the Free plan the row shows a small lock and the word Basic. Click it to see what it does and compare plans.

steps.name: Set a password
steps.text: Type a password of at least 6 characters and press Set password.

steps.name: Turn it on
steps.text: Turn on the switch beside Password. It saves straight away. Send people the address and the password.

steps.name: Change or remove it
steps.text: Type a new password and press Set password to change it. Turn the switch off to remove the password.

gets: A site that asks for a password
Visitors who enter it once and stay signed in for a week
faq: Which plan do I need?
Basic ($3 a month) or above. Every paid plan starts with a 7-day free trial.
How long does a visitor stay signed in?
A week.

title: Put a prototype on your own domain
metaTitle: Put a prototype on your own domain · Aero
description: Connect a domain you own to a site in Aero. Type it in Settings, press Connect and add the DNS records Aero shows. Needs the Solo plan or above.
answer: To put a prototype on your own domain, open its site in Aero, type the domain under Your own domain in Settings and press Connect. Add the two DNS records Aero shows with your registrar. Needs Solo or above.

steps.name: Open the site
steps.text: Go to Sites and open the site. Find Your own domain under Address in Settings. On Free and Basic it shows a small lock and the word Solo.

steps.name: Enter your domain
steps.text: Type a domain you own, like app.yourname.com (Example), and press Connect.

steps.name: Add the DNS records
steps.text: Aero lists an A record and a CNAME record. Add both with your domain registrar.

steps.name: Wait for them to resolve
steps.text: The certificate is issued once the records resolve, and the site is live at your domain.

steps.name: Or pick a shorter Aero address
steps.text: On Basic and up, an HTML site can swap its generated address for a short one, like pocket.aeroapp.ai. Changing it breaks the old link straight away.

gets: Your site on your own domain
A certificate set up for you
faq: Which plan do I need?
Solo ($6 a month) or above. Basic gives you your own aeroapp.ai address instead.
How long does it take?
It depends on how quickly your DNS records resolve.
Can I change the domain later?
Yes. Type the new domain and press Connect. Aero takes the old one off the site.
Can I use an Aero address that is taken?
No. Aero addresses must be unique. If one is taken, Aero says so.

title: See who visits your prototype
metaTitle: Site analytics: see who visits your prototype · Aero
description: The Analytics tab on a site in Aero shows visitors, where they came from, their country and their device. Needs the Solo plan or above.
answer: To see who visits your prototype, open its site in Aero and pick the Analytics tab. It shows visitors and visits, where they came from, their country or city, and their device, browser and system. Needs Solo or above.

steps.name: Open the site
steps.text: Go to Sites and open the site.

steps.name: Go to Analytics
steps.text: Pick the Analytics tab. On Free and Basic it shows a small lock and the word Solo. Click it to see what it does and compare plans.

steps.name: Pick a period
steps.text: Choose Today, 7 days, 30 days, This month or 12 months.

steps.name: Pick a number
steps.text: Visitors, Visits, Pageviews and Visit time each switch the chart. Under it you see views per visit and the bounce rate.

steps.name: Read the lists
steps.text: Where from shows the sources. Place splits by country or city, and Device by device, browser or operating system.

gets: Visitors, visits, pageviews and visit time over time
Where visits came from, by source, country and city
Devices, browsers and operating systems
faq: Which plan do I need?
Solo ($6 a month) or above. Every paid plan starts with a 7-day free trial.
Does it show who the visitors are?
No. It shows numbers, where visits came from and what people used, not who they are.
Are test sessions counted?
No. Analytics counts visits to the live site. Test sessions show in Tests, with a recording of what each tester did and said.

title: Roll back to an earlier version of a site
metaTitle: Roll back to an earlier version of a site · Aero
description: Aero keeps a version each time you publish an HTML site. Open the Versions tab and restore an older one to put it live again.
answer: To roll back a site in Aero, open it and go to Versions. Each publish is a row, and the live one is marked Live. Open the menu on an older row and pick Restore this version.
needs: An HTML site with more than one version. A Figma site shows your live prototype, so it has no versions

steps.name: Open the Versions tab
steps.text: Go to Sites, open the site, then Versions.

steps.name: Find the version
steps.text: Each row shows its date, what changed, how many files, and where it came from, such as a web upload. The live one is marked Live.

steps.name: Open it first if unsure
steps.text: Press a row to open that version and look at it.

steps.name: Restore it
steps.text: Open the row’s menu and pick Restore this version. It goes live at the same address.

steps.name: Drafts
steps.text: Files you add with Publish straight away switched off are saved as a draft. Pick Publish in the row’s menu to make it live, or Discard draft.

gets: An older version live again
Newer versions still listed
faq: Does a restore delete newer versions?
No. They stay in the list as drafts until you discard them.
Does a test change when I roll back?
No. A test keeps its own copy of the version it was made from. Its Setup says which, such as “Testing Pocket, version 4”, and Change makes a separate test from another version.
cta: Publish and go back any time

title: Update a published site
metaTitle: Update a published site at the same address · Aero
description: Publish a new version of a site at the same address. Drop new files on its page in Aero, or paste a prompt into your chat. Every version is kept.
answer: To update a published site, open it in Aero and drop the new files on Drop files, or use Ask Claude or ChatGPT to get a prompt for your chat. The new version goes live at the same address, and the old one is kept.
needs: The new files, or the chat where you built it

steps.name: Open the site
steps.text: Go to Sites and open the site. The Update section is on the Site tab.

steps.name: Drop the new files
steps.text: Drop a folder, a zip or a few files on Drop files, or press Choose files.

steps.name: Publish straight away, or save a draft
steps.text: A dialog lists the files. With Publish straight away on, press Publish and they go live. Switch it off to save a draft and publish it later from Versions.

steps.name: Or ask your chat
steps.text: Ask Claude or ChatGPT gives you a prompt. Paste it into the chat where you built the site and it publishes the next version here.

steps.name: Check the version
steps.text: The new version shows in Versions, marked Live. Restore an older one any time.

alt.p: A Figma site shows your live prototype, so changes you make in Figma show up on their own. There is nothing to upload.

gets: The new version live at the same address
Every earlier version kept, so you can go back
Drafts, when you want to check before going live
faq: Does the address change?
No. Each update becomes the next version at the same address.
Can I check an update before it goes live?
Yes. Switch off Publish straight away and the files are saved as a draft. Open it from Versions, then publish it or discard it.
Do my tests change when I update?
No. A test keeps its own copy of the version it was made from. Make a new test from the site to test the update.
Is there a limit on versions?
Aero keeps every version you publish.
